claim_map.claim: Early Theseus treated state-spill freedom as a guiding architectural ideal and acknowledged that much of the 2017 design was incomplete.
Mature Theseus uses client-owned resource objects, reference-counted sharing, explicit state roots for unavoidable state, and an ownership chain to retain code/data reachable from tasks.
Live replacement is a staged publication protocol around ownership, not an ownership-only operation.
Affine ownership does not prove that independently constructed representations denote disjoint resources; global uniqueness requires checked creation/bookkeeping plus a correct overlap specification.
For Anneal, separate local liveness/retention from global identity and current-generation authority.
claim_map.derivation: Theseus ownership safely retains representation/code lifetimes after a correct identity relation has been established, while its later correctness work shows ownership cannot itself establish resource uniqueness; its live-evolution path separately serializes namespace authority changes.

negative_space: No fresh Theseus execution or benchmark.
No claim that the 2024 RepCreator implementation is merged in the pinned 2024-09-22 source head.
No recommendation of a specific Anneal content digest, distributed reference-count protocol, or Lean invalidation mechanism.
Issue #451 is independent corroboration; exact identity with the bug anecdote in arXiv:2501.00248v1 is a derived match, not an explicit paper citation.
